title: Smart Thermostat Rebates in Ottawa 2026: $125 and a Free Route
desc: Ottawa smart thermostat rebate for 2026: $125 under Home Renovation Savings, Peak Perks for central air, and the free thermostat under the Energy Affordability Program.
lead: Ottawa homeowners can get $125 back on an eligible smart thermostat, and low-income households can get one free. January lows average 13.2°C below zero here, so the heating season matters more than the summer program.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for a smart thermostat in Ottawa
cards_intro: We re-read the three program pages on October 4, 2026. The rebate is province-wide, so the amount is the same in every city, and the page that matters is the one that says whether your home and heating qualify.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: One rebate on an eligible smart thermostat, claimed with a code at checkout or with a receipt uploaded within 60 days of buying.

cards.title: Who is eligible
cards.amount: Gas heat or electric heat or cooling
cards.note: You must be an Enbridge Gas customer heating mainly with a gas furnace or boiler, or be on the Ontario grid and use electric heat or cooling, and live in a house, semi, row, townhome or mobile home on a permanent foundation.

cards.title: One per household, ever
cards.note: A smart thermostat rebate, discount or free device from Enbridge, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings in the past rules you out.

cards.title: Peak Perks
cards.note: A prepaid card for joining the summer demand response program with central air or a heat pump controlled by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat.

cards.title: Energy Affordability Program
cards.note: Households under the income limits get a programmable or smart thermostat, depending on the home, with other upgrades at no charge.

cards.title: Cornwall excluded
cards.note: Cornwall Electric customers cannot join the rebate or Peak Perks.

after_cards: The rebate page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: Where a thermostat earns its keep in Ottawa

Ottawa's average January low is -13.2°C, and the coldest recorded day in our data set reached -32.2°C. Long heating seasons give a schedule more hours to work with than in the warmer southwest of the province. The program does not promise a saving, so treat the rebate as a discount on a tool and the savings as something you earn by setting it well.

Hydro Ottawa supplies electricity to most of the city, and Peak Perks is open to its customers if they have central air or a heat pump with an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat. The program runs summer afternoon events lasting up to three hours that move the setting by up to 2°C. With long winters here, the heating side of the thermostat is where most of its use will be.

The Energy Affordability Program covers postal codes beginning K, L, M, N and P, which includes Ottawa. Income limits for comprehensive support run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four and $107,823 for five or more. Owners and renters who hold the utility account can apply, by phone at 1-844-770-3148 or online. The program says it is fully funded and accepting applications.

Before you buy, press the program page's Get code button, receive a code by email and enter it at checkout on the Home Depot, Best Buy, Copeland Sensi, ecobee or Mysa website. After you buy, press Apply for rebate and upload the receipt within 60 days. Either way the thermostat has to be one of the listed models, and a Ottawa homeowner who buys in a store should keep the receipt.

The most common reason for a refusal is an earlier offer. If you ever received a thermostat, a discount or a rebate on one from Enbridge Gas, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings, the program treats this as a second claim. If you are not sure, look for old emails or ask the program before you buy.
claim_steps: Check that your home type, heating and cooling match the eligibility card, and that you have not had a thermostat offer before.
Pick one of the listed models from ecobee, Google Nest, Honeywell Home, Copeland Sensi, Mysa or Sinopé.
Get a code from the program page and use it at checkout, or buy first and upload the receipt within 60 days.
If you have central air, enroll the same thermostat in Peak Perks. Hydro Ottawa is your local distributor, but Peak Perks is run by Save on Energy.
If your household income is under the program limits, call 1-844-770-3148 before buying, since a free thermostat may be available.
faq: Is there a free thermostat in Ottawa?
Only through the Energy Affordability Program, if your household income is under its limit. The limits run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four.
Will Hydro Ottawa give me a thermostat?
We did not find a free-thermostat offer on the pages we read. Check Hydro Ottawa's own program page for any change.
Does the Ottawa loan program pay for a thermostat?
We have not found that a thermostat is listed there, so ask Better Homes Ottawa before assuming it is.
Can I use Peak Perks with a heat pump?
Yes, if the heat pump is part of central air conditioning and an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat controls it.
